froggy_package.name: opencode-froggy
froggy_package.note: source_commit and checked_paths below describe the 0.12.0 baseline, which is the last version recorded as hook-capable here; see drift_2026_11_10.

drift_2026_11_10.summary: The Froggy hooks.md loader this scaffold targets was removed in opencode-froggy 1.7.0 (published 2026-11-01). The generator still writes .opencode/hook/hooks.md and an unpinned opencode-froggy plugin entry, so a fresh scaffold installs a Froggy that ignores those hooks. Not changed here; needs an owner decision.
evidence: npm tarballs inspected 2026-11-10: opencode-froggy 0.12.0 through 1.6.2 (published 2026-10-24) ship a hooks.md loader (dist/loaders.js and dist/config-paths.js mention hooks.md); 1.7.0 (published 2026-11-01) and 1.8.0 do not.
opencode-froggy@1.8.0 dist/plugin.test.js has the test 'ignores legacy %s hook configuration' (global and project hooks.md must not run) and 'does not register the removed tool automation hooks'.
https://github.com/smartfrog/opencode-froggy README (1.8.0) documents agents, memory and tools only, and says it requires OpenCode V2.

The OpenCode config schema (https://opencode.ai/config.json) marks the `plugin` key deprecated; the current key is `plugins` (https://opencode.ai/docs/config/ and https://opencode.ai/docs/plugins/). The generator still writes `plugin`.
drift_2026_11_10.not_verified: Whether opencode-froggy 1.6.2 runs on the OpenCode release a user has installed (1.0.0+ README says it requires OpenCode V2), and whether OpenCode still accepts the deprecated `plugin` key at runtime.
